pure-announcement.rationale: This is trade-press coverage of the findings of IBM's annual Cost of a Data Breach study, not a product launch, release note or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: No nearest concept (SIEM agentic visibility gap, SLO burn-rate alerting, OSV format, etc.) covers breach-cost economics or extortion tactics, so nothing here is already in the corpus.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Every headline claim is attributed to the linked 2026 IBM report drawn from 602 breached organizations, which a reader can obtain and check.

durability.rationale: The note is dominated by single-year survey figures — $4.99m average, 12% rise, 41% reputation-extortion rate, sector rankings — that the 2027 edition of the same report will supersede wholesale.

actionability.rationale: Its only guidance is IBM's boilerplate (monitor data flows, adopt zero trust), which changes no concrete build or buy decision for a reader.

atomicity.rationale: All the statistics serve one statable claim — breach costs hit a record high, pushed up by AI-driven attacks and reputation-based extortion — with no unrelated ideas bundled in.
